questions.stem: In 165.324, which digit is in the hundredths place?

explanation: After the decimal point the places are tenths, hundredths, thousandths.
In 165.324, the digit 3 is in the tenths place, 2 is in the hundredths place and 4 is in the thousandths place.
The digit in the hundredths place is 2, option (2).

questions.stem: Which two lines are perpendicular to each other?

images.alt: Figure ABCDE drawn on a square grid, with E also joined to C. From A, B is 2 squares right and 2 squares down. From B, C is 1 square left and 1 square down. From C, D is 3 squares left and 1 square down. From D, E is 1 square left and 3 squares up. From E, A is 3 squares right and 1 square up.

explanation: Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle (90°).
AB goes 2 squares right and 2 squares down, so it runs along the diagonals of the grid squares.
BC goes 1 square left and 1 square down, so it runs along the other diagonal of a grid square.
The two diagonals of a square cross at right angles, so AB and BC are perpendicular.
Check the others: AE and CD both go 3 squares across and 1 square up, so they are parallel, not perpendicular. AB and AE, and AE and BC, do not meet at a right angle.
The answer is option (1).

review.note: The grid is warped in the scan, so the corners do not sit exactly on straight grid lines. The positions of A to E were read by following each bent grid line at high zoom.

questions.stem: What is the total volume of water in the two containers?

images.alt: Two measuring containers. The big one is marked 1000 ml at the top and has 10 equal intervals; the water reaches the 7th mark from the bottom. The small one is marked 500 ml at the top and has 10 equal intervals; the water reaches the 2nd mark from the bottom.

explanation: Big container: 1000 ml is divided into 10 equal intervals, so each interval is 1000 ÷ 10 = 100 ml.
The water is 3 intervals below the 1000 ml mark: 1000 − 300 = 700 ml.
Small container: 500 ml is divided into 10 equal intervals, so each interval is 500 ÷ 10 = 50 ml.
The water reaches the 2nd mark from the bottom: 2 × 50 = 100 ml.
Total = 700 + 100 = 800 ml, option (3).

questions.stem: In the number line, what is the value represented by A?

images.alt: A number line from 7 to 9 divided into 8 equal intervals. A is at the 3rd mark after 7.

explanation: From 7 to 9 is 2, and it is divided into 8 equal intervals.
Each interval = 2 ÷ 8 = 0.25.
A is 3 intervals after 7: 7 + 3 × 0.25 = 7.75.
The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: A machine prints 15 postcards in 5 minutes. At this rate, how many postcards can it print in 50 minutes?

explanation: 50 minutes is 50 ÷ 5 = 10 times as long as 5 minutes.
So the machine prints 10 times as many postcards: 15 × 10 = 150.
The answer is option (2).

questions.stem:
Arrange these masses from the lightest to the heaviest.
2.35 kg, 2 kg 50 g, 2{3/10} kg

explanation: Change every mass to kilograms as a decimal.
Compare 2.35, 2.05 and 2.30: the order from lightest is 2.05, 2.30, 2.35.
So the order is 2 kg 50 g, 2{3/10} kg, 2.35 kg, option (4).

questions.stem: How many eighths are there in 3{5/8}?

explanation: 1 whole = 8 eighths, so 3 wholes = 3 × 8 = 24 eighths.
{5/8} is 5 more eighths.
24 + 5 = 29 eighths, option (2).

questions.stem: Round 47 458 to the nearest thousand.

explanation: 47 458 lies between 47 000 and 48 000.
Look at the hundreds digit: it is 4, which is less than 5, so round down.

questions.stem: There are 48 chocolates in a box. 36 of them are milk chocolates while the rest are dark chocolates. What is the ratio of the number of dark chocolates to the number of milk chocolates?

explanation: Dark chocolates = 48 − 36 = 12.
Dark : milk = 12 : 36.
Divide both by 12: 1 : 3.
The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: AB and CD are straight lines. Find ∠m.

images.alt: Straight lines AB and CD cross at a point. A third line goes up from the crossing point, between C and B: it makes 30° with the line to C and 125° with the line to B. A fourth line goes down from the crossing point and makes a right angle with the line to A. Angle m is between this fourth line and the line to D.

explanation: Call the crossing point O. The angle between OC and OB = 30° + 125° = 155°.
AB is a straight line, so the angle between OA and OC = 180° − 155° = 25°.
CD is a straight line, so the angle between OA and OD = 180° − 25° = 155°.
This 155° is made up of the right angle and ∠m: ∠m = 155° − 90° = 65°.
The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Some students were asked to choose their favourite hobby. The pie chart represents their choices. Which hobby was chosen by {1/5} of the students?

images.alt: Pie chart: Jogging 30, Reading 48, Gaming 62, Dancing 40, and Cycling, whose sector has a right angle at the centre.

explanation: The Cycling sector has a right angle, so Cycling is {1/4} of the students.
The other four hobbies make up {3/4} of the students: 30 + 48 + 62 + 40 = 180 students.
{3/4} of the students = 180, so {1/4} = 60 and the total = 4 × 60 = 240 students.
{1/5} of 240 = 48 students.
48 students chose Reading, option (4).

questions.stem: Ali had y marbles. Bala had 5 more marbles than Ali. Charles had 3 times as many marbles as Ali. They had 45 marbles altogether. How many more marbles did Charles have than Bala?

explanation: Ali has y, Bala has y + 5 and Charles has 3y.
Bala has 8 + 5 = 13 marbles. Charles has 3 × 8 = 24 marbles.
Charles has 24 − 13 = 11 more marbles than Bala, option (3).

questions.stem:
Farah glued 64 cubes of side 1 cm to form the solid shown.
[[img1]]
She painted the whole solid red, including the base. How many cubes of side 1 cm have only 2 faces painted red?

images.alt: A large cube made of small cubes, 4 cubes long, 4 cubes wide and 4 cubes high.

explanation: 64 = 4 × 4 × 4, so the solid is a big cube with 4 small cubes along each edge.
A small cube has exactly 2 painted faces when it lies along an edge of the big cube but is not at a corner. (Corner cubes have 3 painted faces.)
Each edge has 4 cubes. Take away the 2 corner cubes: 4 − 2 = 2 cubes with 2 painted faces.
A cube has 12 edges: 12 × 2 = 24 cubes.
The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: Lisa packed 60 cream cookies and 75 mint cookies into as many boxes as possible. She packed the same number of each type of cookies in each box. How many mint cookies were there in each box?

explanation: Every box gets the same number of cream cookies and the same number of mint cookies, so the number of boxes must divide both 60 and 75 exactly.
For as many boxes as possible, find the greatest common factor of 60 and 75.
Factors of 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60. Factors of 75: 1, 3, 5, 15, 25, 75. The greatest common factor is 15, so there are 15 boxes.
Mint cookies in each box = 75 ÷ 15 = 5. (Cream cookies in each box = 60 ÷ 15 = 4.)
The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: The figure is made up of three identical right-angled triangles. The perimeter of the figure is 72 cm. Find the area of the figure.

images.alt: Two right-angled triangles are placed one above the other, sharing a horizontal side, so that their left sides form one straight vertical line 24 cm long and their right corners meet at one point. The slanted side of the top triangle is 20 cm. The third triangle is joined along the slanted side of the bottom triangle, with its right angle at the bottom right of the figure.

explanation: The 24 cm side is made of one side from each of two identical triangles, so that side of each triangle is 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm.
The longest side of each triangle is 20 cm.
The outside of the figure is made of: the 24 cm side, one 20 cm side, and the two shorter sides of the third triangle.
Two shorter sides of the third triangle = 72 − 24 − 20 = 28 cm. One of them is 12 cm, so the other is 28 − 12 = 16 cm.
Area of one triangle = {1/2} × 12 × 16 = 96 cm².
Area of the figure = 3 × 96 = 288 cm², option (3).

questions.stem: Find the value of 11.1 − 0.77

explanation: Write both numbers with 2 decimal places: 11.10 − 0.77.

questions.stem: Ted completed his 1.6 km walk/run in 11 min 40 s. Veronica was faster than Ted by 55 s. What was Veronica's timing? (Type your answer in the form: 12 min 30 s)

explanation: Veronica was faster, so her time is 55 s less than 11 min 40 s.
40 s is not enough to take away 55 s, so change 1 minute into 60 seconds: 11 min 40 s = 10 min 100 s.

questions.stem: Find the perimeter of a quarter circle of radius 7 cm. (Take π = {22/7})

explanation: A quarter circle has one curved edge and two straight edges, each a radius.
Two straight edges = 7 + 7 = 14 cm.
Perimeter = 11 + 14 = 25 cm.

questions.stem: Johann took 15 minutes to walk from home to school at an average speed of 70 m/min. How far was school from home? Give your answer in km.

explanation: Distance = speed × time = 70 m/min × 15 min = 1050 m.
School was 1.05 km from home.

review.note: Resolved on review (answer differs from or goes beyond the printed key; the stored answer was re-checked): The answer blank on the question paper is printed with the unit km, so the answer should be 1.05 km. The answer key gives 1050, which is the distance in metres. The working is the same; only the unit differs. Stored answer is 1.05 km. Check whether 1050 (m) should also be accepted.

questions.stem:
The line graph shows the height of a plant measured from March to August.
[[img1]]
What was the height of the plant in May?

images.alt: Line graph of the height of a plant in cm. The vertical axis goes from 0 to 160 in steps of 20, with a grid line every 5 cm. Mar 35, Apr 70, May 95, Jun 105, Jul 130, Aug 140.

explanation: On the vertical axis there are 4 small intervals between 80 and 100, so each small interval is 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm.
The point for May is one small interval below 100.

questions.stem: The square grid shows the positions of eight points.

images.alt: Square grid with eight points and an arrow showing north pointing up. Counting columns from the left and rows from the top: A is at column 1, row 1. B is at column 5, row 1. C is at column 6, row 2. H is at column 1, row 3. E is at column 3, row 3. F is at column 2, row 4. D is at column 4, row 4. G is at column 2, row 6.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Fill in the blanks with north, south, east or west.
F is ______ of D and ______ of G.
(Type the two words separated by a comma.)
explanation: F and D are on the same horizontal grid line. F is to the left of D, and left is west. So F is west of D.
F and G are on the same vertical grid line. F is above G, and up is north. So F is north of G.
The answers are west and north.

parts.prompt: Write down all possible points that are south-west of B. (Type the letters separated by a comma.)
explanation: South-west is exactly halfway between south and west. From B, move 1 square left and 1 square down each time, along the diagonals of the squares.
1 step: no point. 2 steps: E. 3 steps: F. 4 steps: no point.
The points south-west of B are E and F.

questions.stem: The ratio of the length of a rectangle to its breadth is 7 : 3. The length of the rectangle is 12 cm longer than its breadth. Find the length of the rectangle.

explanation: Length = 7 units and breadth = 3 units.
Difference = 7 − 3 = 4 units = 12 cm.
1 unit = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 cm.
Length = 7 × 3 = 21 cm.

questions.stem:
Find the average of the following numbers:
101, 0, 125, 74

explanation: There are 4 numbers. The 0 still counts as one of the numbers.
Average = 300 ÷ 4 = 75.

questions.stem: The square grid shows lines ST and TU, which are two sides of a trapezium. ∠TSV = 90°. Draw trapezium STUV and label the vertices clearly. Ensure precision in your drawing. (Draw it on your canvas, then check.)

images.alt: Square grid with two lines. ST goes from S to T, 6 squares to the right and 2 squares down, and has an arrowhead mark on it to show a parallel side. TU goes from T to U, 2 squares to the right and 4 squares down. S is 3 squares from the left edge and 1 square from the top edge of the grid.

answer.value: V is 1 square to the left of S and 3 squares below S. Join S to V and V to U. Side VU is parallel to ST, and the angle at S is a right angle.

explanation: The arrowhead on ST shows that ST is one of the parallel sides, so the fourth side UV must be parallel to ST.

ST goes 6 squares right and 2 squares down, which is 3 right for every 1 down. A line at right angles to it goes 1 across for every 3 down. So from S, the line SV goes 1 square left and 3 squares down each time.
From U, go backwards parallel to ST: 3 squares left and 1 square up each time. After 3 such steps (9 left, 3 up) you reach the point that is 1 square left and 3 squares below S.
That point is V. Draw SV and VU. STUV is a trapezium with ST parallel to VU and ∠TSV = 90°.

review.keyAnswer: Drawing: V is 1 square left and 3 squares below S; VU parallel to ST
review.solvedAnswer: V is 1 square left and 3 squares below S

questions.stem: Pamela builds a solid using 8 cubes of side 1 cm. The side view is shown.

images.alt: On the left, a solid made of cubes with arrows marking the front view and the side view. The front row has 2 cubes side by side. Behind the right-hand cube is 1 more cube. Behind that is a back row of two stacks: a stack 2 cubes high on the left and a stack 3 cubes high on the right. On the right, the side view drawn on a dot grid: three squares in a row at the bottom, with two more squares stacked on top of the right-hand square.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Draw the top view on the grid. (Draw it on your canvas, then check.)

answer.value: 5 squares: a row of 2 squares, then 1 square below the right-hand square, then another row of 2 squares below that. It looks like a rectangle 2 squares wide and 3 squares long with the middle square on the left side missing.

explanation: The top view shows only where there are cubes when you look down from above. Stacks of cubes look like one square.
Front row: 2 cubes side by side, so 2 squares.
Middle row: only 1 cube, behind the right-hand cube, so 1 square.
Back row: two stacks (2 high and 3 high), so 2 squares.
The top view has 5 squares: 2 squares, 1 square on the right, 2 squares.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Pamela wants to build a cuboid of sides 3 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm. How many more cubes does she need?
explanation: Each cube has side 1 cm, so the cuboid needs 3 × 3 × 4 = 36 cubes.
She already has 8 cubes.
More cubes needed = 36 − 8 = 28.

review.keyAnswer: a) top view drawn: 2 squares, 1 square, 2 squares  b) 28
review.solvedAnswer: a) 5 squares in rows of 2, 1, 2  b) 28
review.note: In the picture the stack at the back left is partly hidden. It is 2 cubes high: 2 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 8 cubes, which matches the 8 cubes stated.

questions.stem: Mrs Chong has 2 rolls of ribbon each {9/10} m long. She cuts the ribbon into equal pieces to make bows. Each piece is {1/5} m long. How many bows can she make?

explanation: {1/5} m = {2/10} m, so each bow needs {2/10} m of ribbon.
One roll is {9/10} m. {9/10} ÷ {2/10} = 9 ÷ 2 = 4 remainder 1, so one roll gives 4 pieces with {1/10} m left over.
The left-over bits are too short for a bow and they are on separate rolls, so they cannot be used.
2 rolls give 2 × 4 = 8 bows.

questions.stem: After a 10% discount, the price of an admission ticket to the amusement park is $45. Children are given a further discount of $3. What is the percentage discount for one child ticket?

explanation: After a 10% discount, $45 is 90% of the usual price.
10% of the usual price = $45 ÷ 9 = $5, so the usual price = $50.
A child pays $45 − $3 = $42.
Total discount for a child = $50 − $42 = $8.
Percentage discount = {8/50} × 100% = 16%.

questions.stem:
At a movie marathon, John watched movies one after another without any break in between. He started to watch the first movie at 18 30. At what time did he start to watch the 4th movie? (Give your answer in 24-hour clock)
[[table1]]

explanation: The 4th movie starts when the first three movies have ended.
Time for the first three movies = 1 h 20 min + 50 min + 1 h 30 min = 2 h 100 min = 3 h 40 min.
He started the 4th movie at 22 10.

questions.stem:
The table shows the first 3 rows of a number pattern.
[[table1]]
In which column and which row will number 498 appear? (Type your answer in the form: Column B, Row 7)

explanation: Each row has 4 numbers and the numbers snake: odd rows go from left to right, even rows go from right to left.
Look at the biggest number in each row: Row 1 has 6, Row 2 has 10, Row 3 has 14. The biggest number is 4 × (row number) + 2.
498 − 2 = 496 and 496 ÷ 4 = 124, so 498 is the biggest number in Row 124.
Row 124 is an even row. In even rows (like Row 2) the numbers go from right to left, so the biggest number is in Column A.
498 is in Column A, Row 124.

questions.stem: A baker had 300 eggs at first. In the morning, he used some eggs. In the afternoon, he used {1/3} of the remaining eggs. After that, there were 60 eggs left. How many eggs did the baker use in the morning?

explanation: In the afternoon he used {1/3} of the remaining eggs, so {2/3} of the remaining eggs were left.
{2/3} of the remaining eggs = 60, so {1/3} = 60 ÷ 2 = 30.
Eggs remaining after the morning = 3 × 30 = 90.
Eggs used in the morning = 300 − 90 = 210.

questions.stem: There are 7 shaded squares in the figure. Shade 5 more squares to form a symmetric figure with AB as the line of symmetry. (Shade the squares on your canvas, then check.)

images.alt: A grid of 6 rows and 6 columns of squares. The dotted line AB runs along the diagonal from the bottom-left corner (A) to the top-right corner (B). Counting rows from the top and columns from the left, the shaded squares are: row 1 column 6; row 2 columns 2 and 5; row 3 columns 1 and 5; row 4 column 5; row 5 column 3.

answer.value: Counting rows from the top and columns from the left, shade these 5 squares: row 2 column 3, row 2 column 4, row 4 column 2, row 5 column 5 and row 6 column 4.

explanation: The line of symmetry AB works like a mirror. Each shaded square must have a partner the same distance away on the other side of AB.
The squares at row 1 column 6 and row 2 column 5 lie on the line AB, so they are their own partners.

Flip each of the other shaded squares over AB: row 2 column 2 goes to row 5 column 5. Row 3 column 1 goes to row 6 column 4. Row 3 column 5 goes to row 2 column 4. Row 4 column 5 goes to row 2 column 3. Row 5 column 3 goes to row 4 column 2.
None of these 5 partner squares is shaded yet, so shade them: row 2 columns 3 and 4, row 4 column 2, row 5 column 5 and row 6 column 4.

review.keyAnswer: Shaded: row 2 columns 3 and 4, row 4 column 2, row 5 column 5, row 6 column 4
review.solvedAnswer: row 2 columns 3 and 4, row 4 column 2, row 5 column 5, row 6 column 4

questions.stem: There were 50 red pens and 230 blue pens. After an equal number of red and blue pens were added, the ratio of the number of red pens to the number of blue pens became 1 : 3. How many red pens were there in the end?

explanation: The same number of pens was added to both colours, so the difference between them stays the same.
Difference = 230 − 50 = 180.
In the end, red : blue = 1 : 3, so the difference is 3 − 1 = 2 units.
2 units = 180, so 1 unit = 90.
Red pens in the end = 1 unit = 90. (Check: 40 pens were added to each, giving 90 red and 270 blue, and 90 : 270 = 1 : 3.)

questions.stem: Siti had 35 marbles and Ted had more marbles than her. After giving Siti m marbles, Ted had 20 more marbles than Siti. How many marbles did Ted have at first? Give your answer in terms of m in the simplest form.

explanation: After receiving m marbles, Siti had 35 + m marbles.
Ted then had 20 more than Siti: 35 + m + 20 = 55 + m marbles.
Before that, Ted had given away m marbles, so at first he had 55 + m + m marbles.
Ted had 2m + 55 marbles at first.

questions.stem: A cyclist and a motorist started travelling at the same time from point A to point B. The motorist's average speed was 16 km/h faster than the cyclist. When the motorist reached point B in 12 minutes, the cyclist had only travelled {3/5} of the distance. What was the cyclist's average speed in km/h?

explanation: In {1/5} h the motorist travels {1/5} × 16 = 3.2 km more than the cyclist.
In that time the motorist covered the whole distance and the cyclist covered {3/5} of it, so the extra 3.2 km is {2/5} of the distance.
{1/5} of the distance = 3.2 ÷ 2 = 1.6 km, so the cyclist travelled {3/5} of the distance = 3 × 1.6 = 4.8 km.
Cyclist's speed = 4.8 km ÷ {1/5} h = 4.8 × 5 = 24 km/h.

questions.stem: A box contained some yellow cubes and 72 blue cubes. 40% of the cubes were yellow. After some red cubes were added into the box, 32% of the cubes were yellow. How many red cubes were there?

explanation: At first 40% of the cubes were yellow, so 100% − 40% = 60% were blue.
60% = 72 cubes, so 10% = 12 cubes. Yellow cubes = 40% = 4 × 12 = 48. Total at first = 10 × 12 = 120 cubes.
The number of yellow cubes did not change. After the red cubes were added, the 48 yellow cubes were 32% of all the cubes.
Red cubes = 150 − 120 = 30.

questions.stem: The figure shows the net of a cuboid with 2 square faces. The ratio of the length to the breadth is 3 : 2. The perimeter of the figure is 128 cm. Find the volume of the cuboid.

images.alt: Net of a cuboid made of 6 faces arranged like steps going down to the right. Top row: a square, then a rectangle lying flat. Middle row, starting under the rectangle: a rectangle lying flat, then a square. Bottom row, starting under that square: two upright rectangles side by side.

explanation: Length : breadth = 3 : 2. Each square face is 2 units by 2 units and each rectangular face is 3 units by 2 units.

Go around the outside of the net and add up the sides in units. Top edge: 2 + 3 = 5. Going down the right-hand side in steps: 2, 2, 2, 2, then 3. Bottom edge: 2 + 2 = 4. Going back up the left-hand side in steps: 3, 3, 2, 2, 2.
32 units = 128 cm, so 1 unit = 4 cm.
The cuboid is 12 cm long (3 units), 8 cm wide and 8 cm high (2 units each).
Volume = 12 × 8 × 8 = 768 cm³.

questions.stem: After Aini gave {1/6} of her stickers away and Bala gave {1/4} of his stickers away, both of them had the same number of stickers left. The total number of stickers Aini and Bala gave away was 2280. How many stickers did Bala have at first?

explanation: Aini had 1 − {1/6} = {5/6} of her stickers left. Bala had 1 − {1/4} = {3/4} of his stickers left.
These amounts are equal, so make the numerators the same: {5/6} = {15/18} and {3/4} = {15/20}.
So Aini had 18 units at first and Bala had 20 units at first, and each had 15 units left.
Aini gave away 18 − 15 = 3 units. Bala gave away 20 − 15 = 5 units. Together: 3 + 5 = 8 units.
Bala at first = 20 × 285 = 5700 stickers.

questions.stem: At a concert, there were 30% more women than men and 25% more boys than girls. There were 250 people at the concert with as many males as females. How many girls were there at the concert?

explanation: Males = females = 250 ÷ 2 = 125.
30% more women than men: men = 10 units, women = 13 units. 25% more boys than girls: girls = 4 parts, boys = 5 parts.
Males: 10 units + 5 parts = 125. Females: 13 units + 4 parts = 125.
Compare the two: the females have 3 more units but 1 fewer part, and the totals are equal. So 1 part = 3 units.
Males: 10 units + 5 parts = 10 units + 15 units = 25 units = 125, so 1 unit = 5.
1 part = 3 × 5 = 15. Girls = 4 parts = 4 × 15 = 60.
Check: men 50, women 65, girls 60, boys 75. Males = 50 + 75 = 125 and females = 65 + 60 = 125.

questions.stem:
The figure shows two rectangular tanks X and Y at first. Tank X contained 432 cm³ of water and tank Y was empty.
[[img1]]
Water dripped at a rate of 3 cm³ per second from a leaking tap at the bottom of tank X into tank Y. How long did it take for the height of the water level in tank Y to be 3 cm above that of tank X?

images.alt: Tank X stands on a table and holds water to a height of 9 cm. A tap at the bottom of tank X drips into tank Y, an empty rectangular tank on the floor with a base 8 cm long and 3 cm wide.

explanation: Base area of tank X = 432 ÷ 9 = 48 cm². Base area of tank Y = 8 × 3 = 24 cm².
When 48 cm³ of water moves from X to Y, the level in X drops by 48 ÷ 48 = 1 cm and the level in Y rises by 48 ÷ 24 = 2 cm. So the gap between the two levels changes by 1 + 2 = 3 cm.
At first the water in X is 9 cm higher than in Y. In the end the water in Y is 3 cm higher than in X. The gap must change by 9 + 3 = 12 cm.
12 ÷ 3 = 4, so 4 × 48 = 192 cm³ of water must move. (Check: X has 432 − 192 = 240 cm³, height 240 ÷ 48 = 5 cm. Y has 192 cm³, height 192 ÷ 24 = 8 cm. 8 − 5 = 3 cm.)
Time = 192 ÷ 3 = 64 seconds.

review.note: The answer blank has no unit printed; the answer is given in seconds, as in the key. The heights compared are the depths of water in each tank.

questions.stem: The line graph shows the volume of water the Tan family used from January to June.

images.alt: Line graph of the amount of water used in m³. The vertical axis goes from 0 to 60 in steps of 10, with a grid line every 2 m³. Jan 34, Feb 48, Mar 28, Apr 40, May 50, Jun 24.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What was the percentage increase in the water used from April to May?
explanation: From the graph, April = 40 m³ and May = 50 m³.
Increase = 50 − 40 = 10 m³.
Percentage increase is compared with April's amount: {10/40} × 100% = 25%.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
The table shows the charges for water usage.
[[table1]]
How much did the Tan family pay for their water bill in May?
explanation: In May the family used 50 m³.
Additional water = 50 − 40 = 10 m³: 10 × $4.50 = $45.

questions.stem: ABCD is a parallelogram and CFDE is a rhombus. ∠ADG = 12°.

images.alt: Parallelogram ABCD with AB on top and DC below. Rhombus CFDE has DC as its diagonal, with E above AB and F below DC. Side DE crosses AB at G and side CE crosses AB at H. Angle DFC is 74°. Angle ADG, between DA and DE, is 12°. Angle w is at H, between HE and HB. No angle y is marked.

parts.label: a
explanation: Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal, so ∠DEC = ∠DFC = 74°.
All sides of a rhombus are equal, so ED = EC and triangle EDC is isosceles: ∠ECD = (180° − 74°) ÷ 2 = 53°.
AB is parallel to DC, so ∠EHG = ∠ECD = 53° (corresponding angles).
∠w and ∠EHG are on the straight line AB: ∠w = 180° − 53° = 127°.

parts.label: b

answer.value: This part cannot be answered: ∠y is not marked anywhere in the figure on the question paper, and the answer key also says 'Not labelled in question paper'.

explanation: Look for ∠y in the figure: only ∠w, the 12° angle and the 74° angle are marked.
Because ∠y is not shown, there is no way to tell which angle is wanted.

questions.stem: 1 m white lines are painted on roads as lane markings. The 7 white lines before a traffic light crossing are 1 m apart while the other white lines are 3 m apart. The distance between two traffic light crossings along a straight stretch of two-lane road is 493 m.

images.alt: A two-lane road between two traffic light crossings, with arrows showing traffic moving from left to right. A row of 1 m white lines runs along the middle. The first white line starts at the left crossing and the lines are 3 m apart. Near the right crossing the last 7 white lines are 1 m apart and the last line ends at the crossing.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many 1 m white lines are there between the two traffic light crossings?
explanation: Look at the last 7 white lines before the crossing. They have 6 gaps of 1 m between them: 7 × 1 m + 6 × 1 m = 13 m.
Length of the rest of the road = 493 − 13 = 480 m.
On this part, each white line is followed by a 3 m gap. One line and one gap make a group of 1 + 3 = 4 m.
Number of groups = 480 ÷ 4 = 120, so there are 120 white lines on this part.
Total = 120 + 7 = 127 white lines.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: George and Hariz started jogging at the same time but in opposite directions on a sidewalk from one traffic light crossing to the other traffic light crossing. George's speed was 5 m/s and Hariz's speed was 4 m/s. Both of them did not change their speeds throughout. After jogging for 1 minute, how far apart were George and Hariz from each other?
explanation: They started at opposite crossings, 493 m apart, and jogged towards each other.
1 minute = 60 seconds. George jogged 5 × 60 = 300 m and Hariz jogged 4 × 60 = 240 m.
Together they covered 300 + 240 = 540 m, which is more than 493 m. So they had already passed each other.
Distance apart = 540 − 493 = 47 m.

review.note: The road picture is blurry. At high zoom it shows a white line starting at the left crossing, lines 3 m apart, and 7 lines 1 m apart with the last one ending at the right crossing; part (a) uses this layout, as the key does. In part (b) the two joggers are taken to start from opposite crossings and jog towards each other, as the key does.

questions.stem: The bar graph shows the number of books borrowed from the school library over five days. The bar for Friday is not shown.

images.alt: Bar graph of the number of books borrowed: Mon 65, Tue 90, Wed 85, Thu 40. The bar for Fri is replaced by a question mark.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
The books borrowed were fiction and non-fiction books. 30% of the books borrowed from Monday to Thursday were non-fiction books. The table shows the number of fiction books borrowed from Monday to Thursday. The number of fiction books borrowed on Wednesday is not shown.
[[table1]]
How many fiction books were borrowed on Wednesday?
explanation: Read the bars: Mon 65, Tue 90, Wed 85, Thu 40. Total from Monday to Thursday = 65 + 90 + 85 + 40 = 280 books.
30% were non-fiction, so 100% − 30% = 70% were fiction.
Fiction books on Mon, Tue and Thu = 45 + 57 + 28 = 130.
Fiction books on Wednesday = 196 − 130 = 66.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The number of books borrowed from Monday to Wednesday is 4 times as many as the number of books borrowed on Thursday and Friday. Find the number of books borrowed on Friday.
explanation: Books borrowed from Monday to Wednesday = 65 + 90 + 85 = 240.
This is 4 times the number for Thursday and Friday, so Thursday and Friday together = 240 ÷ 4 = 60.
Thursday = 40, so Friday = 60 − 40 = 20 books.

review.note: The page is slightly tilted in the scan, so the dotted guide lines slope. Following them at high zoom, the bars read Mon 65, Tue 90, Wed 85 and Thu 40, the same values the key uses.

questions.stem: The average height of a group of 3 girls and 5 boys was 160 cm. The average height of the 3 girls was 12 cm less than the average height of the 5 boys. Find the average height of the 5 boys.

explanation: Total height of the 8 children = 8 × 160 = 1280 cm.
Suppose each girl were 12 cm taller. Then the girls' average would be the same as the boys' average.
The total would go up by 3 × 12 = 36 cm: 1280 + 36 = 1316 cm.
Now all 8 children have the boys' average height: 1316 ÷ 8 = 164.5 cm.
The average height of the 5 boys is 164.5 cm. (Check: girls' average = 152.5 cm. 3 × 152.5 + 5 × 164.5 = 457.5 + 822.5 = 1280.)

questions.stem: Mr Abdul received some Majulah Singapura vouchers in denominations of $2, $5 and $10. There were as many $10 vouchers as $5 vouchers. The ratio of the number of $2 vouchers to the number of $10 vouchers was 3 : 2. The value of all the vouchers was $1260.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What was the total value of the $2 vouchers he received?
explanation: Number of $2 vouchers : number of $10 vouchers = 3 : 2, and there are as many $5 vouchers as $10 vouchers. So $2 : $5 : $10 = 3 : 2 : 2.
Make one group of 3 $2 vouchers, 2 $5 vouchers and 2 $10 vouchers.
Number of groups = 1260 ÷ 36 = 35.
Each group has $6 worth of $2 vouchers: 35 × $6 = $210.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
After a month, Mr Abdul had 4 $2 vouchers, 2 $5 vouchers and 1 $10 voucher left. He bought some food from 3 different stalls. Payment was made at each stall using vouchers, cash or a combination of both. The value of the vouchers used at each stall cannot be more than the cost of the food. What was the least amount he could have paid in cash?
[[table1]]
explanation: Total cost of food = $8 + $9 + $11 = $28. Total value of vouchers = 4 × $2 + 2 × $5 + $10 = $28. To pay no cash, every voucher would have to be used exactly.
The $10 voucher is too big for Stall A ($8) and Stall B ($9), so it can only be used at Stall C. $11 − $10 = $1, and no other voucher fits in the $1 left, so Stall C needs $1 cash.
Now use the 4 $2 vouchers and 2 $5 vouchers for Stall A ($8) and Stall B ($9). Stall B: $5 + $2 + $2 = $9, no cash.
Vouchers left: one $5 and two $2. For Stall A the best is $5 + $2 = $7 (adding another $2 would make $9, more than $8), so Stall A needs $1 cash.
Cash can only be reduced in whole dollars and the vouchers cannot make $27 (there is no $1 voucher) or fit $28 exactly, so the least cash is $1 + $1 = $2.

review.note: The table in part (b) has a single heading 'Cost of Food' across both columns on the paper; it is transcribed with the headings 'Stall' and 'Cost of Food'.

images.alt: Figure 1: three identical upright rectangles side by side forming one long rectangle. A shaded triangle has its base along the bottom of the first rectangle, from the bottom-left corner of the figure to the bottom of the first dividing line, and its third corner at the top-right corner of the figure. One more line is drawn from the bottom of the first dividing line to the top of the second dividing line.

Figure 2: three circles in a row, touching, with the line AB through their centres. Each circle has a square with one corner at the centre of the circle and the opposite corner pointing down outside the circle; two sides of the square are radii of the circle. First circle: the circle is shaded except for the part covered by the square, and the whole square is unshaded. Second circle: the circle is unshaded and the whole square is shaded. Third circle: the whole circle is shaded and only the part of the square outside the circle is unshaded.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Figure 1 shows three identical rectangles. The area of the shaded triangle is 256 cm². Find the difference in area between the shaded and unshaded parts.
[[img1]]
explanation: The base of the shaded triangle is the bottom side of one rectangle and its height is the height of the rectangle.
Area of the triangle = {1/2} × base × height = {1/2} of the area of one rectangle. So one rectangle = 2 × 256 = 512 cm².
Area of the three rectangles = 3 × 512 = 1536 cm².
Unshaded area = 1536 − 256 = 1280 cm².
Difference = 1280 − 256 = 1024 cm².

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Figure 2 is formed by three similar-sized circles and three similar-sized squares. Line AB passes through the centre of the three circles. The area of each square is 256 cm². Find the difference in area between the shaded and unshaded parts. (Take π = 3.14)
[[img2]]
explanation: 16 × 16 = 256, so each square has side 16 cm. Two sides of each square are radii, so the radius of each circle is 16 cm.
The part of each square inside its circle is a quarter circle: {1/4} × 3.14 × 16 × 16 = 200.96 cm². The part of each square outside its circle = 256 − 200.96 = 55.04 cm².
Shaded: first circle 3 quarter circles, second figure 1 whole square, third circle 4 quarter circles. Shaded = 7 × 200.96 + 256 = 1406.72 + 256 = 1662.72 cm².

Unshaded: first figure 1 whole square (256), second circle 3 quarter circles (3 × 200.96 = 602.88), third figure the part of the square outside the circle (55.04). Unshaded = 256 + 602.88 + 55.04 = 913.92 cm².
